config.description: Two processes on two cores. Four QUBO variables. This is the fastest deterministic end-to-end default-pipeline sanity check.
config.name: Minimal preset direct path

config.description: Three processes on two cores. Six QUBO variables. Verifies the normal direct path with a non-trivial one-hot assignment.
config.name: Three-process direct path

config.description: Four processes on two cores use exactly eight variables, equal to qubit_max. This verifies the <= boundary stays on DefaultPipeline.
config.name: Direct path at qubit boundary

config.description: Generated uniform workload with explicit num_processes. This verifies the runner's generated workload mode without using sweep expansion.
config.name: Generated static workload direct path

config.description: Uses a deliberately low penalty to inspect feasible optimum vs unconstrained optimum reporting. This is a diagnostic, not a success-claim scenario.
config.name: Low-penalty ground truth diagnostic

config.description: Balanced three-process workload where brute force should be available, letting the runner report candidate energy, global energy, and optimality gap.
config.name: Optimality gap sanity

config.description: Uniform weights create many equivalent feasible schedules. Returned assignments must still be exactly one core per process.
config.name: One-hot feasibility under degeneracy

config.description: Uses the standard X mixer on a direct workload. This intentionally samples infeasible states and validates fallback/feasibility reporting against the XY mixer scenarios.
config.name: X mixer feasibility stress

config.description: Four processes on three cores. Tests K > 2 variable mapping, decoding, brute-force validation, and visualization metadata.
config.name: Three-core direct assignment

config.description: Four processes on two cores require eight variables, so qubit_max six should force the iterative sub-QUBO path.
config.name: Minimal forced decomposition

config.description: Six-process iterative run using WEIGHT_DESCENDING. This isolates the simple size/weight partition heuristic.
config.name: Weight-descending decomposition

config.description: Same six-process workload as T3.2, but with COUPLING_DESCENDING. Useful for comparing heuristic output and final global energy.
config.name: Coupling-descending decomposition

config.description: Eight processes on two cores with qubit_max six should produce at least three sub-QUBOs and exercise phi propagation over multiple iterations.
config.name: Multi-sub-QUBO stress

config.description: Five processes on three cores with qubit_max nine. Tests iterative extraction and decoding when K > 2.
config.name: Three-core iterative decomposition

config.description: Six-process direct run with qubit_max equal to 12. Repeats the same static configuration to collect repeated QAOA measurements without sweep expansion.
config.name: Medium direct repeated baseline

config.description: Six-process direct run with qubit_max equal to 12. Repeats the same static configuration to collect repeated QAOA measurements without sweep expansion.
config.name: Medium direct repeated baseline

config.description: Six-process direct run with qubit_max equal to 12. Repeats the same static configuration to collect repeated QAOA measurements without sweep expansion.
config.name: Medium direct repeated baseline

config.description: Same six-process workload as T4.1 but forced through iterative decomposition. Compare global energy, load imbalance, and solve time against the direct baseline.
config.name: Medium iterative repeated comparison

config.description: Same six-process workload as T4.1 but forced through iterative decomposition. Compare global energy, load imbalance, and solve time against the direct baseline.
config.name: Medium iterative repeated comparison

config.description: Same six-process workload as T4.1 but forced through iterative decomposition. Compare global energy, load imbalance, and solve time against the direct baseline.
config.name: Medium iterative repeated comparison

config.description: Generated ten-process workload on two cores. Static scaling check for runner-generated input and iterative scheduling without live tracing.
config.name: Generated larger iterative workload

config.description: Captures current system processes, forces a two-core virtual scheduling target, and runs the automatic direct/iterative path. Non-deterministic by design.
config.name: Live trace small core count

config.description: Real system snapshot during external CPU-intensive activity for thesis-style evidence on realistic processes. Non-deterministic by design.
config.name: Live trace realistic load
